dimension: North & West Shore Tahoe independent / mid-size resorts (Mt Rose, Diamond Peak, Homewood, Granlibakken, Sky Tavern, Tahoe XC, + Tahoe Donner as a bonus North Shore independent)

findings.name: Homewood Mountain Resort — OPERATING STATUS FOR 2026-27
findings.claim: Homewood IS planning to operate for 2026-27, and it is the biggest status change in Tahoe this year. Its own season pass page says 'We can't wait to welcome everyone back to the West Shore for the 2026-2027 winter!' and 2026-27 passes are on sale now. Caveats worth telling friends: (1) Homewood was fully CLOSED for 2024-25, (2) it reopened for 2025-26 but had a badly truncated season — it could not open on its planned Dec 12, 2025 date due to lack of snow and then closed early on March 17-18, 2026, (3) the whole mountain is currently a construction site (gondola install started May 1, 2026; Madden Chair removed), and (4) as of 2026-08-28 Homewood has published NO 2026-27 lift ticket prices — its tickets page literally says '2026-2027 Lift Ticket Products and information coming Fall 2026.' Treat Homewood as a real but higher-risk option for a group trip you are booking now.
findings.restrictions: Day-ticket products not yet announced; mountain under active construction; history of late openings and early closures
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~3h45m–4h15m / ~220 mi (I-680 → I-80 → Truckee → CA-89 S through Tahoe City) — estimate, not routing-verified

findings.name: Homewood Mountain Resort — new gondola on track for 2026-27
findings.claim: Homewood's new 8-passenger gondola is reported on schedule for a December 2026 completion and a 2026-27 opening. Homewood's own gondola page lists 'Gondola Opening GOAL: Winter 2026-2027' with the building permit complete and installation in process. Homewood also says the gondola will lift the beginner terrain ~1,000 ft higher up the mountain — relevant because your group includes beginners.
findings.restrictions: Stated as a goal/schedule, not a guarantee; the gondola was already delayed a full year once

findings.name: Homewood — Unlimited Season Pass (2026-27)
findings.claim: Unlimited Pass, no blackout dates: Adult $1,299; Teen $899; Junior $699; Senior $949; Family Pass (2 adults + 2 junior/teen) $3,699. Adult/Senior Unlimited holders can buy 6 unrestricted buddy day tickets per year.
findings.restrictions: None (no blackouts). Non-refundable, non-transferable. Age determined as of 12/1/2026.

findings.name: Homewood — Value Season Pass (2026-27)
findings.claim: Value Pass, valid 7 days a week excluding peak holidays: Adult $899; Teen $699; Junior $599; Senior $749. Peak (blacked-out) dates: Dec 26 – Jan 1, Jan 16 & 17, Feb 13-15.
findings.restrictions: Blacked out Dec 26–Jan 1, Jan 16-17 (MLK), Feb 13-15 (Presidents)

findings.name: Homewood — Weekly 2-Day midweek pass (2026-27)
findings.claim: 'Weekly 2-Day' pass — any two MIDWEEK days per week all season: Adult $799; Senior $649. Homewood calls this 'our best value.' Peak/blackout dates for this product are ALL Saturdays and Sundays plus Dec 21–Jan 1, Jan 18, and Feb 15-19.
findings.restrictions: MIDWEEK ONLY — all weekends blacked out. Bad fit for a Saturday friends trip; good only if your crew can take weekdays off.

findings.name: Homewood — Inspire & Serve discounted day ticket
findings.claim: $75 non-peak day ticket for Lake Tahoe Basin first responders, Lake Tahoe Basin teachers, and active-duty & retired military. Requires a pay stub dated August 2025 or newer for eligibility. This is the ONLY specific day-ticket dollar figure Homewood has published for the upcoming season.
findings.restrictions: Non-peak days only; eligibility limited to first responders/teachers (Tahoe Basin) and military. Page does not state which season this rate is for.

findings.name: Homewood — on-site rentals
findings.claim: Homewood operates an on-site rental shop with a new Atomic ski fleet and carries Atomic, Nordica, Burton, Jones and Moment, plus premium demos from two local brands. NO PRICES ARE PUBLISHED on the rentals page — I could not confirm a single dollar figure for Homewood rentals for any season.
findings.restrictions: Rental shop confirmed to exist; pricing unpublished as of 2026-08-28

findings.name: Diamond Peak — 2026-27 Public Season Pass, Preseason tier
findings.claim: 2026-27 season passes are ON SALE NOW at the Preseason tier (valid 5/1/2026 – 10/31/2026): Adult (24-64) $588; Youth (13-23) $495; Child (7-12) $282; Senior (65-69) $519; Super Senior (70-79) $282; 6-and-under and 80+ free. Passes also include spring access for the remainder of the prior season. Prices rise to the 'Prewinter' tier on Nov 1.
findings.per_day_usd: $73.50/day at 8 days; $58.80/day at 10 days — beats your $60/day gold standard at 10+ days
findings.restrictions: Buy by Oct 31, 2026 for this price. Age determined by age on Dec 1. Diamond Peak offers a 'Peak Pledge' no-hassle refund policy on unused passes. Renewing holders who reuse their card get $10 off.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~3h45m–4h15m / ~235 mi (I-80 to Truckee → CA-267 → CA-28 to Incline Village) — estimate

findings.name: Diamond Peak — 2026-27 Public Season Pass, Prewinter tier
findings.restrictions: Price jumps $145 vs. buying before Oct 31 — a real deadline worth flagging to the group

findings.name: Diamond Peak — Transferable Season Pass (2026-27)
findings.claim: $1,269 for a fully unrestricted, fully TRANSFERABLE season pass — you can share it with anyone. Limited quantities. This is genuinely interesting for a friend group: one $1,269 pass shared among a rotating crew works out cheap per skier-day, though only one person can use it on a given day. It carries NO pass perks (no buddy tickets, no bonus days at partner resorts, no on-mountain discounts) and no further discounts apply.
findings.per_day_usd: $63/day if used 20 days across the group; $42/day at 30 days
findings.restrictions: One user per day. Limited quantity, typically on sale May/June. No perks. Existing regular-pass holders can upgrade by paying the difference (call 775-832-1177).

findings.name: Diamond Peak — 2026-27 peak period dates
findings.claim: Diamond Peak's published 2026-27 PEAK periods are: Dec 19, 2026 – Jan 3, 2027; Jan 16-18, 2027; Feb 13-21, 2027. Everything else is either 'Value' (Mon-Fri non-peak) or 'Weekend' (Sat/Sun).
findings.restrictions: These dates drive both ticket and rental pricing tiers

findings.name: Diamond Peak — single-day lift tickets (LAST SEASON'S 2025-26 rates)
findings.claim: LAST SEASON (2025-26) online rates — 2026-27 day-ticket prices are NOT yet published. Adult (24-64): $137 Value / $169 Weekend / $179 Peak. Youth (13-23) and Senior (65-79): $116 / $147 / $163. Child (7-12): $53 / $74 / $84. Beginner ticket (School House + Lodgepole chairs only): $77 / $109 / $119. 6-and-under and 80+ free. Buying at the resort window costs $10 MORE than these online prices. No half-day tickets offered.
findings.per_day_usd: $137 midweek / $169 weekend — well above your $60/day baseline
findings.restrictions: Expect 2026-27 rates to be published in the fall and likely higher. The $77 Beginner ticket is a notable option for first-timers in your group.

findings.name: Diamond Peak — Flex Passes (2- and 3-day multi-packs, LAST SEASON'S rates)
findings.claim: This is Diamond Peak's answer to your Boreal 4-pack. 2025-26 pricing: 2-Day Flex — Adult $289 ($145/day), Youth/Senior $279 ($140/day), Child $138 ($69/day). 3-Day Flex — Adult $399 ($133/day), Youth/Senior $369 ($123/day), Child $189 ($63/day). Valid ANY day with NO BLACKOUTS, days need not be consecutive, and after first pickup they are direct-to-lift (skip the ticket line). Flex passes typically go on sale in NOVEMBER, so 2026-27 pricing is not out yet.
findings.per_day_usd: $133/day adult — more than double your $60/day gold standard
findings.restrictions: No blackouts, but non-transferable, non-refundable, and unused days do NOT roll over. Can be upgraded to a season pass at the ticket window on first day of use.

findings.name: Diamond Peak — reload discount on tickets and flex passes
findings.claim: If you originally bought online and keep the RFID ticket media card, you can reload it online for an additional $5 off the already-discounted online price — for a 1-day ticket, 2-day flex, or 3-day flex, regardless of what you originally bought. You must log in with the same account. Losing the card costs a $5 (flex: $5) new-media fee.
findings.restrictions: Requires original online purchase and the physical card; free 6-&-under / 80+ tickets cannot be reloaded online

findings.name: Diamond Peak — ON-SITE rental equipment
findings.claim: Full on-site rental shop at the base. Online booking prices (walk-up at the resort is $10 more): Adult package (13+, skis/boots/poles/helmet or board/boots/helmet) $65 Value / $80 Weekend / $80 Peak. Child package (12 & under) $55 / $70 / $70. Helmet only $10/$15/$15. Ski or snowboard boots only $37. Skis or snowboard only $42. Demo package $90 / $105 / $105. A $250 credit card deposit is required for all rentals. This table sits directly under the '2026-27 PEAK PERIODS' header, so it most likely reflects 2026-27 rates, but the page also still carries a 'Closed for the 2025-26 season' banner — treat the season label as slightly ambiguous.
findings.restrictions: $250 CC deposit. Walk-up +$10. Book online for faster service and better price.

findings.name: Diamond Peak — lockers and tuning (group logistics)
findings.claim: Smartecarte day lockers $13–$20 (must clear by 4:30pm). Overnight lockers $30 plus $30 key deposit, fit three pairs of adult skis and boots, available until 10am next day. Tuning: rub-on wax $5, hot wax $20, basic tune $42, complete tune $60, binding test $20. There is also a satellite rental/ticket shop — the Hyatt Sport Shop at the Hyatt Regency Lake Tahoe, 111 Country Club Drive, Incline Village — where you can pick up lift tickets and rentals and book group lessons for ages 7+.
findings.restrictions: Day lockers must be emptied by 4:30pm daily

findings.name: Mt. Rose Ski Tahoe — Select Pass (2026-27) — BEST per-day value found on the North Shore
findings.claim: $375 adult (16+) for a full season on ONE midweek day of your choosing, every week. Void dates: Nov 27-28, Dec 18–Jan 2, Jan 18 (MLK), Feb 15 (Presidents). If you use it ~12 times that's $31/day; ~15 times is $25/day — roughly half your $60/day Boreal gold standard. No child version listed.
findings.restrictions: Locked to ONE self-chosen non-weekend day per week, all season. Useless for a Saturday group trip. Adults only (16+).
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~4h–4h30m / ~245 mi (I-80 to Reno, then NV-431 Mt Rose Hwy) — estimate; highest base elevation in Tahoe

findings.name: Mt. Rose — Off-Peak Season Pass (2026-27)
findings.claim: New-buyer price: Adult $675, Child (6-15) $265. Renewal price: Adult $475, Child $215. Full season pass with weekends voided during Jan and Feb only — you get weekends in Nov, Dec, Mar and Apr, then midweek-only in Jan/Feb. Void dates: Nov 27-28, Dec 18–Jan 2, Jan 16-17, Feb 13-15, plus all Sat/Sun in Jan & Feb.
findings.per_day_usd: $67.50/day at 10 days new; $47.50/day at 10 days renewal
findings.restrictions: All January and February weekends voided — that's the heart of the season for a weekend crew

findings.name: Mt. Rose — Classic Season Pass (2026-27)
findings.claim: New-buyer price: Adult $875, Child (6-15) $365. Renewal price: Adult $675, Child $315. Valid nearly every day with only holiday void dates: Nov 27-28 (Thanksgiving), Dec 26-30 (Christmas), Jan 16-17 (MLK), Feb 13-15 (Presidents). This is the sweet spot pass if your group wants ordinary weekends.
findings.restrictions: Only 4 short holiday void windows; all other Saturdays and Sundays are valid

findings.name: Mt. Rose — Premier Season Pass (2026-27)
findings.claim: New-buyer price: Adult $1,075, Child (6-15) $465. Renewal price: Adult $875, Child $415. No void dates at all. NOTE: OnTheSnow lists Mt Rose Premier at $1,175 adult / $515 child for 2026-27 (updated April 2026) — that conflicts with the resort's own page. Trust skirose.com; the OnTheSnow figure may be a later price tier or stale.
findings.restrictions: No blackouts. Mt Rose has no senior pricing at all — only Adult 16+ and Child 15-and-under.

findings.name: Mt. Rose — Two'fer Tuesday (closest thing to your 4-pack math)
findings.claim: Two lift tickets for the price of one, every non-holiday Tuesday — 2 adult full-day OR 2 child full-day. Buyable online in advance or at any ticket window day-of; it never sells out. Both tickets must be used that same Tuesday and the second is not valid on a different day. Must be 'like-priced' tickets (two adults, or two kids); mixing adult + child defaults to the higher rate. For a paired-up group this effectively halves the day rate — historically this landed around $60-80/person, which is right at your gold standard.
findings.per_day_usd: ~half the prevailing adult day rate per person
findings.restrictions: Tuesdays only, non-holiday. Not combinable with other offers. Does not apply to Tyke tickets. Season of the current terms not stated on the page.

findings.name: Mt. Rose — other named daily specials
findings.claim: Mt Rose runs a special almost every day of the week, all non-holiday: Bonus Monday (discounted Monday ticket if you show a lift ticket from the previous Sat/Sun, must buy onsite) plus discounted Monday tickets for hospitality workers (restaurant/lodging/airline/bar staff, show a check stub, work ID or business card); Two'fer Tuesday; Ladies' Day Thursday at $79 for women; 'Ski G.I.F.' discounted PM half-day after 12:00pm Fridays; Sleep-in Saturdays discounted PM half-day after 12:00pm on select Saturdays; Locals' Sunday (discounted with local ID showing residence within a 1-hour drive — Bill would NOT qualify from San Jose). Also: active military $79 full-day at the window, veterans $109, and 'Ski the Day You Fly' $79 with a same-day RNO boarding pass.
findings.restrictions: All excluded during holiday periods. Locals' Sunday requires ID showing residence within 1 hour of Mt Rose — a San Jose group does not qualify. These dollar figures are live on the page now but the page does not state which season they apply to.

findings.name: Mt. Rose — ticket reload discount (up to 25% off)
findings.claim: Mt Rose has no traditional multi-pack or punch card, but it does have a reload: keep your ticket card, scan the QR code on the back, and reload it online through the dynamic calendar for your next visit — 'Reloads can save up to 25% on lift tickets on your next trip.' You can also apply the full cost of a day's lift ticket toward a season pass at Guest Services at the end of your ski day.
findings.restrictions: Requires keeping the physical ticket card and reloading online; savings amount is 'up to' 25% and varies with the dynamic calendar

findings.name: Mt. Rose — NO multi-pack / punch card exists
findings.claim: I could not find any Mt. Rose 4-pack, 5-pack, punch card, or multi-day ticket product. Their own ticketing page pushes you toward (a) dynamic online pricing bought by midnight the day before, (b) daily specials, (c) the reload discount, or (d) a season pass. This is a genuine structural gap vs. your Boreal 4-pack.
findings.restrictions: Negative finding — absence of a product, verified across the lift-tickets, daily-specials and season-pass pages

findings.name: Mt. Rose — window (walk-up) day ticket rate
findings.claim: Mt Rose uses fully dynamic pricing and does NOT publish a fixed 2026-27 day rate. Two anchors: (1) their own lift-ticket page still carries the note '2024/25 Full price tickets $189 Adults/$95 Kids' for day-of window purchases; (2) OnTheSnow lists a 2025-26 weekday rate of $119 adult / $59 child (last updated Oct 31, 2025). Online tickets must be purchased by midnight the day before to get the discounted rate; otherwise you pay full window price. Same-day tickets can only be bought at the ticket windows, and Mt Rose says it never sells out of lift tickets. Tyke tickets (5 & under) are $20, resort-only.
findings.price_usd: $189 adult / $95 child (2024-25 window); $119 adult / $59 child (2025-26 weekday, OnTheSnow)
findings.per_day_usd: $119–$189 adult depending on channel and season
findings.restrictions: Dynamic pricing; 2026-27 figures unavailable as of 2026-08-28. Online cutoff is midnight the night before.

findings.name: Mt. Rose — ON-SITE rental equipment
findings.claim: On-site rentals on the lower level of the Main Lodge, and you can add them to your online lift ticket purchase. Adult (16+): $59 one day / $99 two days at the resort; $54 one day / $89 two days ONLINE. Child (4-15): $29 one day / $49 two days. Helmet $10. Poles $10. Ski boots only + required binding release test $100. Ski package = skis, boots, poles; snowboard package = board and boots. Largest ski/snowboard boot size 16; largest board 170 wide. Season equipment leases are also available but are exclusive to pass holders.
findings.restrictions: Prices live on the page now but season not labeled. Season lease program is pass-holders only.

findings.name: Mt. Rose — group rates for a big crew
findings.claim: Mt Rose offers group discounts, but the threshold is high: 'typically 40+' people, designed for bus groups. Requires a single group leader and one payment, with 48-hour advance reservation preferred. Call 775-849-0704. Also relevant for a group: season pass holders get 2 discounted buddy tickets ($40 off adult / $20 off child at the on-site rate).
findings.restrictions: 40+ people needed for the group rate — almost certainly too large for a friends trip

findings.name: Granlibakken Tahoe — ski hill day tickets
findings.claim: Tahoe's cheapest lift access, but it is a tiny beginner hill: ~300 ft vertical, 2 surface lifts (a rope tow for the bunny slope and a Poma button lift for the intermediate slope), no chairlifts, roughly 2 runs. Published rates (from a Tahoe City rental agency page dated Jan 2026, i.e. the 2025-26 season): Weekend/Holiday adult $45, child 12-and-under $35; Weekday/Non-holiday adult $40, child $30. Granlibakken's own official page does not display a price table — it links out to a 'BUY TICKETS' booking widget. Lodging guests at Granlibakken get 50% off ski AND sled tickets.
findings.per_day_usd: $40 midweek / $45 weekend — below your $60/day gold standard
findings.restrictions: Ski hill and ski school open FRIDAY–MONDAY only outside of peak periods; lifts run 7 days/week during peak season and holidays. Beginner-to-low-intermediate terrain only. 2025-26 holiday windows on that page were Dec 20–Jan 1 and Feb 14-23. Prices are from a third-party page, not the resort's own.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~3h30m–4h / ~215 mi (I-80 to Truckee → CA-89 S to Tahoe City) — estimate; 725 Granlibakken Rd, Tahoe City

findings.name: Granlibakken — on-site rentals and lodging-guest discount
findings.claim: Rentals available on-site in the historic Ski Hut at the base — alpine ski/snowboard, plus cross-country and snowshoe gear — and the shop explicitly lets you take the gear to OTHER ski areas, which is unusual and useful. Third-party listing quotes $40 adult / $35 child (12 & under) per day with helmets $6 extra; I could NOT verify these on Granlibakken's own site. Granlibakken does NOT rent snow boots, snow pants or jackets — nearest source is Tahoe Dave's, 1.5 miles away in Tahoe City. Parking at Granlibakken is free. Lodging guests get 50% off ski and sled tickets, and the on-site restaurant is Rusty's American Lunch in the Ski Hut, typically 11am-3pm when lifts run.
findings.restrictions: Rental prices are third-party sourced and unverified against the resort; season unknown. Gear may be used at other ski areas.

findings.name: Granlibakken — best use case for your group
findings.claim: Granlibakken is a lodging resort with a ski hill attached, not a ski resort with lodging. Its real value to a Bay Area group is as an affordable BASE: 74 acres, hotel rooms through multi-bedroom townhomes, a fully-staffed managed sled hill, cross-country and snowshoe access to Paige Meadows, and free parking — sitting a short drive from Palisades Tahoe, Homewood, Northstar, Sugar Bowl and Boreal. They advertise exclusive lodging-partner lift ticket discounts at Palisades Tahoe for guests. If any of your friends are true first-timers, doing a day on Granlibakken's $40-45 hill before a bigger mountain is a legitimately cheap way to de-risk the trip.
findings.restrictions: Lodging-guest ticket discount is 50%; the Palisades lift ticket discount amount is not published

findings.name: Sky Tavern — NOT a public ski area; wrong fit for this trip
findings.claim: Sky Tavern is a Reno nonprofit (501c3) youth learn-to-ski area on Mt Rose Highway, about a mile below Mt Rose. It does NOT sell general-public day tickets. Access is by season membership only, and every membership is valid ONLY on Learn-to-Ski-and-Ride program days — 8 winter weekends, families choosing Saturday, Sunday or both. Critically, an adult affiliated with a registered child is REQUIRED to register and volunteer. This is a family/community program, not a destination for a group of adult friends from San Jose.
findings.restrictions: No public day tickets. Volunteer obligation. Program-day-only access. 21130 Sky Tavern Rd, Reno NV.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~4h–4h30m / ~243 mi (same road as Mt Rose) — estimate

findings.name: Sky Tavern — 2026-27 (their '2027') membership prices
findings.claim: Youth memberships all $299 for the season: Sky Kids/Grommets (ages 4-7), Learn to Ski or Snowboard (8-17), Bus Program (9-17, plus $18 per bus ride, vouchers bought online by Wednesday 5pm for the following weekend), and the new Teen Mountain Volunteer Program (12-17). Adult: Lift Riding Volunteer Adult Membership $275 (8 weekends, volunteer 2 hours, ski 5). An 'Integrity Pass' exists for adults who cannot or do not wish to volunteer — limited availability, price not published on the page. Rentals are NOT included in any membership; a separate season lease is offered. A promo earlier in 2026 included a free Freeride Pass (stated $459 value, ~30 bonus non-program days) with memberships purchased by May 31, 2026 — that window has closed.
findings.restrictions: Adult membership requires a volunteer position. Valid only on program days. Rentals extra. May 31, 2026 Freeride Pass bonus has expired.

findings.name: Tahoe XC (Tahoe Cross Country, Tahoe City) — 2026-27 prices CONFIRMED
findings.claim: Nordic only — no downhill. 2026-27 pricing is published and passes are on sale. Adult season pass $399 (on sale until Nov 9); Youth 13-18 $99; Kids 0-12 FREE; Senior 70-75 $119; Seniors 76+ FREE; Dog season pass $139; Lifetime Legacy Pass (age 70+, one-time, valid for life) $399. Day-ticket MULTI-PACKS: 5-Day Flex Pack $220 ($44/day) and a 10-Pack $440 ($44/day) which saves $110, is FULLY TRANSFERABLE and does NOT expire — the transferable, non-expiring 10-pack is the single most group-friendly product I found in this whole dimension. There is also a 'Glide Pass' ($225, adults 19+, only 40 available) giving all-season use of the on-site rental fleet — skis, poles, boots or snowshoes — though it does NOT include trail access, so you still need a day ticket or season pass.
findings.price_usd: $440 for a 10-pack; $399 adult season pass; $225 Glide rental pass
findings.restrictions: Day tickets must be bought IN PERSON — not sold online or in advance — and single day tickets are non-refundable and non-transferable (the 10-pack, by contrast, IS transferable and never expires). Everyone on the trail system needs a ticket or pass, including dogs. Adult season passes include 2 comp day tickets, Tahoe City Winter Sports Park access, and 2 day tickets at Tahoe Donner XC (not valid weekends or holidays).

findings.name: Tahoe Donner Downhill — 2026-27 season pass (BONUS: strongest North Shore value I found)
findings.claim: Not on your list but it belongs in the comparison — Tahoe Donner is a North Shore independent, is the closest of these to San Jose, is explicitly marketed as a beginner/family mountain, and just opened a brand-new ski lodge. CONFIRMED 2026-27 public (non-member) rates: Adult (18-59) unrestricted $676; Junior (7-17) $436; Child (6 & under) $129. Member rates are much lower (Adult $421) but require Tahoe Donner property ownership. A 2026-27 Combo pass covering BOTH the downhill resort and the 100km cross-country center is $919 public adult / $492 junior. Passes are on sale now at the lowest price of the year; there was an Aug 18 price increase noted.
findings.per_day_usd: $67.60/day at 10 days; $56/day at 12 days — crosses under your $60/day gold standard at ~12 days
findings.restrictions: Unrestricted (no blackouts) for the public adult pass. 2026-27 holiday peak dates: Dec 26-Jan 2, Jan 16-18, Feb 13-20. Ages as of Dec 31, 2026. Note prices already rose once on Aug 18, 2026.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~3h15m–3h45m / ~200 mi (I-680 → I-80 to Truckee) — estimate; the shortest drive of any resort in this set and comparable to your current Boreal drive

findings.name: Tahoe Donner Downhill — day tickets and group rates
findings.claim: 2026-27 day-ticket dollar figures are NOT published yet. What IS published: advance-purchase discounts of 'up to 25% off the window rate,' and member day passes 'starting at $55 per day for adults.' Public advance online pricing is stated to always beat day-of window rates. Group rates ARE available for groups of 20 or more paying participants — a much more realistic threshold than Mt Rose's 40+. Note a policy change: Tahoe Donner no longer offers advance purchase of guest lift tickets by members; guests should just buy online at the public rate.
findings.restrictions: Group rate needs 20+ paying participants. Public pays more than the $55 member floor.

findings.name: Tahoe Donner Downhill — ON-SITE rentals
findings.claim: Full on-site rental shop at the Downhill Ski Resort with fitting help; rent for a day, weekend or longer. Public rates: Adult package (13+, alpine or snowboard) $59 regular / $63 peak; with helmet $71 / $75. Child (12 & under) & Senior (60+) package $44 / $48; with helmet $56 / $60. Demo ski package $69 / $78. Helmet alone $17. Member rates are lower (adult $54). The peak-date footnote on this page still lists 2025-26 dates, so the rates shown may be last season's.
findings.restrictions: Page's peak-holiday footnote references 2025-26 dates, so treat the season as unconfirmed. 'All prices subject to change.'

findings.name: Indy Pass 26/27 — SOLD OUT, not an option this season
findings.claim: The 26/27 Indy Pass (2 days each at 300+ independent areas, plus 25% off a third day) SOLD OUT in 37 minutes during its April 3, 2026 public sale. It is not currently purchasable, so it should not be part of your plan for this winter. Separately, none of Mt Rose, Diamond Peak, Homewood or Granlibakken appear as Indy partners — the Tahoe-area Indy resort that has been named is Donner Ski Ranch (added for 25/26), which is on your I-80 corridor.
findings.restrictions: Sold out April 3, 2026. Historical 24/25 pricing for reference was $419 Base / $539 Indy+ adult.

coverage_gaps: Mt. Rose 2026-27 SINGLE-DAY LIFT TICKET PRICES: could not confirm. Mt Rose uses a dynamic pricing calendar and publishes no fixed table. Their own page still cites 2024/25 window rates ($189 adult / $95 child) and OnTheSnow carries a 2025-26 weekday rate ($119 adult / $59 child). The live price calendar lives at secure.skirose.com, which is blocked by this environment's network egress proxy, so I could not read actual 2026-27 dates. Recommend pulling up skirose.com/lift-tickets and picking a specific target date to get the real number.

Diamond Peak 2026-27 SINGLE-DAY and FLEX PASS prices: not yet published. The lift ticket page's tables are explicitly labeled '2025-26'. Diamond Peak states flex passes typically go on sale in November, so 2026-27 multi-pack pricing should appear around Nov 2026. Their 2026-27 online store returned no lift ticket products at all (off-season).

ALL DRIVE TIMES ARE ESTIMATES. I did not use a routing/traffic service — these are free-flow estimates from mileage and route knowledge (San Jose via I-680/I-80). Real winter times run substantially longer with Sunday-afternoon I-80 traffic, Donner Pass chain controls, or NV-431 Mt Rose Highway closures, which hit Mt Rose and Sky Tavern hardest since NV-431 is a high, exposed summit road.

Season-labeling ambiguity flagged inline on three items: Diamond Peak's rental table (sits under a 2026-27 peak-period header but the page still shows a 2025-26 closed banner), Mt Rose's rental and daily-specials dollar figures (live on the site now but with no season stated), and Tahoe Donner's rental table.

I did not research San Jose / South Bay rental shops for pick-up-before-you-drive gear, since this assignment was scoped to on-site rental availability at each resort.
